newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas rises as within-day market trades heavily.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas rises as within-day market trades heavily.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market saw trade centred around the short term market on Monday, with a spate of deals done on both the within-day and day-ahead markets at higher prices, traders and brokers said.

But little trade was seen further forward. Only two trades, one for June and one for the third quarter, were confirmed done, and dealers said the market had been extremely quiet except on the prompt market.

A single trade for 865,000 therms on the within day market at St Fergus was by far the largest deal done on the prompt market, and the seller speculated that the purchase indicated a significant supply problem, probably offshore.
Apart from this trade, another player did 465,000 therms on the within day market and 300,000 on the day ahead market in several different deals.
Prices for within day gas fluctuated between 10.50 pence and 11.50 pence a therm, witht he day ahead trading between 10.60 and 10.80 pence.

The short term market had moved up over the weekend, with flexibility mechanism system buys done at a System Marginal Price (SMP) of 0.4003 p/kWh on Saturday and 0.4001 p/kWh on Monday morning, around 11.73 pence a therm on both days.
"Demand is relatively high, it's well supported on prompt and there's not a lot of prompt gas around," a trader said.
Following Transco's announcement that it will sell up to 102 million therms of Balancing Margins gas out of storage by the end of April, there was no sign of prices slipping, as some had anticipated.
But the volume of deals done was so small for all except the prompt period that it may not be possible to gauge the effect of the sale on spot markets until volumes pick up again.
Trade on the IPE futures market was thin.
Only 20 lots were traded in three separate deals. The trades done gave few signals to the market: of the three deals, one was slightly firmer, one weaker and one unchanged.

Demand remained strong as temperatures remained well below seasonal normal levels. Transco, the pipeline arm of BG plc, said that Tuesday's temperature is forecast at 6.6 Celsius agaiunst a seasonal normal 10.3 Celsius, and demand is expected to reach 248 mcm, 58 percent of peak day demand.
